title: Care and cleaning
summary: How to clean a gun safely after shooting and after rain, how to store it, and why Sporting™ and Compak® Sporting shooters book a yearly service.

body.html: Cleaning starts with safety. Make sure the gun is unloaded: open it and look into both chambers. Move all cartridges away from your work area, so that you cannot put one into the gun by mistake.

Take the gun apart: remove the fore-end, then the barrels from the action. If you have interchangeable chokes, unscrew them with the choke key; they are cleaned separately (see Pattern testing and choke care).

html: Clean the bores after each day of shooting.
Wet them with a cleaning solvent and run a bore brush (a small wire brush on a rod) through a few times.
Push clean cloth squares (patches) through on the rod until they come out nearly clean.
Finish with a very thin film of oil, and wipe the bore dry before you shoot again.

body.html: Wipe the outside metal with a cloth and a drop of oil to protect it from fingerprints and moisture. Do not soak a wooden stock in oil, because it soaks into the wood. Lightly grease the hinge and the places where the barrels lock into the action, with gun grease.

After rain, dry the gun at once, at the ground or at the hotel. Do not leave a wet gun overnight in a soft slip or a closed case: the moisture stays there for a long time and rust follows. Dry it, wipe it, oil it.

Store the gun dry, in a safe or as your country's law requires; many laws also ask you to keep cartridges separately. Many gunsmiths suggest storing a gun horizontally or with the muzzles down, so that oil does not run into a wooden stock. Do not use steel wool or abrasives: they scratch the finish.

Once a year, or after a large number of shots, take the gun to a gunsmith for a service. After reassembly do not test the gun on a competition stand. In Parcours de Chasse – Sporting™ and Compak® Sporting a test shot is fired only on a separate test stand, where the ground provides one.

key_points.html: First make sure the gun is unloaded and the cartridges are away.
Clean the bores after each day of shooting; oil lightly.
Dry a wet gun at once; do not leave it in a slip overnight.
Store it dry and locked, horizontally or muzzles down.
A yearly service by a gunsmith; test shots only on a test stand.

did_you_know.html: Primers once contained corrosive salts, and a gun had to be cleaned the same day or the bore would rust. Modern primers are non-corrosive, but cleaning after shooting is still a good habit.

quiz.q: What must you do first before cleaning a gun?

options.text: Grease the hinge and the hooks
Check that the gun is unloaded

quiz.explain: Safety first: open the gun and check both chambers.

quiz.q: What should you not do after shooting in the rain?

options.text: Wipe the gun with a dry cloth
Leave it in its slip overnight
Dry the barrels inside and out
Put a thin film of oil on the metal

quiz.explain: Moisture stays in a closed slip for a long time, and rust follows.

quiz.q: Where can you test-fire your gun before a competition?

options.text: On a test stand, if the ground has one
Anywhere on the ground, away from people
In the car park by the clubhouse

quiz.explain: The rules forbid test shots on the competition stand; a separate test stand is used for that.
